analyst_view.overall: Lyon (4th, 20 pts) host Monaco (8th, 17 pts) on Sunday evening, and both play in Europe on Thursday: Lyon at home to Lillestrom in the Europa League, Monaco at Hearts in the Conference League. Lyon won 1-0 at Lille in new coach Carlos Vicens' first game but have scored only 4 league goals in their last six; they are without Pavel Sulc (meniscus), Tyler Morton and Mohamed Ouedraogo. Filipe Luis' Monaco are winless in six Ligue 1 games (back-to-back 1-1 draws) and miss Aleksandr Golovin, Ansu Fati and Stanis Idumbo. The numbers list no missing players for either side, so these absences are not in them, though most are weeks old and partly in the form; no referee is named yet and no dedicated preview for this match was out, so news is thin. With attacking players missing on both sides and both squads playing three days earlier, I lean a little lower on goals only.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, 1.6 for Lyon, and they list nobody missing. Lyon lack Sulc and have scored just 4 in six, and Monaco are without Golovin and Ansu Fati while drawing 1-1 week after week; with both sides coming off European games on Thursday, I lean slightly lower, 2.8 to about 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners, already raised for Lyon's 38 corners in their last six. Both sides play wide (Lyon with Nuamah, Monaco with wing-backs and Detourbet), which their ratings already know, so I stay at about 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards, already trimmed because both sides have been booked less than usual lately (9 cards each in six). No referee is named yet and there is no rivalry or discipline news, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.0 shots, with Monaco's figure trimmed for a quieter recent run. Rotation after Thursday's European games could go either way for shot volume, and both teams carry the same load, so I stay at 25.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target, fairly even between the sides. Lyon kept a clean sheet at Lille in Vicens' first game and Monaco's Balogun leads their line as usual, both in line with what the numbers expect, so I stay at about 9.
